item.title: Livestock Update
item.description:
This month's update brings a major refresh to farming with the introduction of new Livestock animals, critters, and swimmers. Plus, fresh food recipes, the new Biofuel Generator, an overhaul to Sandbag Barricades, and new Powergrid Lootrooms to plunder. And all the usual bug fixes, improvements, and QoL changes!

01 October 2026
DEVBLOG
⠀
LIVESTOCK
This patch we are introducing cows and sheep.

What resources can THEY GIVE?

Both produce dung , cows produce milk, and sheep produce wool .
They can also be harvested for meat, bones and leather like any other animal.
Additionally, you can sell a grown animal to an NPC in the ranch.

How to set up a farm?

There are multiple ways to capture wild livestock, some more efficient than others, but they should all be pretty intuitive.

When the new navmesh is enabled, NPCs can enter player structures and respect doors opening/closing, so the sky is the limit.

Like plants, they have genetics and needs, and can be bred to hunt for a god clone.
However, the genes won't behave exactly like plants, so old techniques may not apply.

WILL IT TANK PERFORMANCE?

Each game frame, only a subset of the NPCs are processed, up to a hardcoded max time per frame.

So when we increase the population, the server doesn't directly lose FPS, instead NPCs just become slower to react because we distribute the load across frames automatically when over budget.

We still spent time multithreading and optimising the new navigation system, at least doubling its performance since the last patch.

As usual, we'll be monitoring server performance and fixing problems as they appear.
Livestock economy
Growing and caring for your livestock will allow you to access some new resources and rewards.

Grown Cattle and Sheep can be sold at a Stable for a variety of resources. Simply lead your animal to the Stables and speak to the new vendor outside, where you will receive a randomized offer based on the gene quality of the animal. You can reject the offer and get another two more times, at which point the vendor will get annoyed and won't want to buy the animal for 15 minutes.
Wool can be harvested from Sheep and traded in to the same vendor, where you will get up the three offers just like when you sell animals. In this case the rewards offered will be based on how much wool you bring in the one go - the maximum being 400. High risk, high reward.
Milk
Cows give you access to a new resource - milk. It can be consumed as is, but if you refrigerate it for 4 hours, you will gain a new option to skim the milk. Skimming the milk will give you two items - Skimmed Milk and Cream. Cream is a more powerful consumable.
Milk and Cream can also be used in a variety of crafting recipes. Milk will generally increase the duration of tea effects, while Cream can be used to increase the potency of those effects.
livestock fencing
To help keep your new livestock under control, we've added new animal gate and fence deployables - perfect for keeping your pet animals safe (ish!).
Biofuel Generator
A way to finally make use of raw or spoiled meat. The Biofuel Generator converts organic matter to low grade, but it must be stirred by hand!

You can fill it up, stir it and let it process. It will take around 30~ minutes before you'll have to stir again, but don't worry - you can hook up some IO to let you know it needs stirring even when you're in the next room.

The amount of low grade you're given depends on the type of organic matter you put in, those with a larger calorific value will give you more low grade.
Critters and Swimmers
Alongside the livestock, we are bringing in some smaller animals to make the world feel more alive! Frogs, Rabbits, Squirrels, Sea turtles, Crabs, and Jellyfish will all be appearing around the island in the biomes that suit them.

Performance

The critters are heavily budgeted and have dedicated behaviours to ensure they don't take up any more server (and client) performance than strictly necessary. For now, they are mostly set dressing, and their performance limits are set with that in mind.
Air wolf repairable helipad
At the start of the wipe the Air Wolf helipad in Bandit Camp will now be in a state of disrepair. The air vehicle vendor NPC will refuse to sell vehicles to anyone until the helipad is repaired.
Repairing the helipad is a process similar to constructing siege weapons - a certain amount of resources are required and you can transfer resources from your inventory by bashing the helipad with a hammer. Once the helipad is repaired it stays repaired for the duration of the wipe.

The intention is that repairing the helipad requires a communal effort and air vehicles purchased from this vendor should no longer start spawning too quickly into the start of the wipe. If a clan wishes to get quick access to air vehicles they are required to invest a significant amount of resources to do so and they are also opening up access to the vendor to everyone else on the server.
Server admins can change this behaviour via convars vehicle.padrepairsrequired (if false this change is effectively reverted) and vehicle.setrepairablepads (force helipad into fully disrepaired/repaired state with 0/1)
sandbag stacking
Sandbags have been reworked. They now have four stages, and each stage is upgraded to the next by stacking another sandbag deployable on top. Each stage grows taller, with the final stage being a pillbox version. All Sandbag skins are supported across all variations.


The crating cost of the sandbag deployable has been reduced to account for needing to stack more of them. When found in loot, Sandbag Barricades will now be a stack of 4. We've also increased the total stack size to 20.
POWERGRID LOOT ROOMS

Building on the Powerplant loot room introduced in the Power Trip update, we’ve added new loot rooms to many other monuments. These rooms are locked by default and become accessible once enough Heavy Fuses have been inserted into the Powerplant to generate the required power. UpdateIkJobData: 0ms → 0.11ms = +0.11ms~

What resources can THEY GIVE?

Both produce dung , cows produce milk, and sheep produce wool .
They can also be harvested for meat, bones and leather like any other animal.
Additionally, you can sell a grown animal to an NPC in the ranch.

How to set up a farm?

There are multiple ways to capture wild livestock, some more efficient than others, but they should all be pretty intuitive.

When the new navmesh is enabled, NPCs can enter player structures and respect doors opening/closing, so the sky is the limit.

Like plants, they have genetics and needs, and can be bred to hunt for a god clone.
However, the genes won't behave exactly like plants, so old techniques may not apply.

Each game frame, only a subset of the NPCs are processed, up to a hardcoded max time per frame.

- We have a lot more control over existing IK, we previously relied heavily on built-in IK from Unity.

Faster:
Update: 1.99ms → 1.47ms = -0.52ms~
LateUpdate: 0.98ms → 0.27ms = -0.71ms~
AnimationGraphFinish: 0.99ms → 0.75ms = -0.24ms~

Worse:
DirectorUpdateAnimationBegin: 0.42ms → 0.62ms = +0.20ms~
UpdateIkJobData: 0ms → 0.11ms = +0.11ms~

Overall:
UpdateScene: 9.36ms → 8.29ms = -1.07ms~
Director begin+end: 1.41ms → 1.37ms = -0.04ms~

Performance-wise, the new IK saves us around 1ms of frame time with 100 players in the scene, this will probably be a lot less drastic if you play on a lower-population server and only end up seeing 5-10 players at once.
Rust Render Pipeline
Because Rust has been around for so long, we were still using Unity’s old Built-in Render Pipeline, which has worked for the most part but has been very limiting in the optimisations we can apply and the effects we can render.

We have now migrated to the new Rust Render Pipeline, which is a custom Scriptable Render Pipeline made specifically for Rust by our graphics team. This gives us a lot more control over the rendering of Rust as a whole. This wasn’t easy, as we had to remake almost every effect in the game to work with this new pipeline.

The main benefit of this will be performance. At first, you should see slightly better performance in most areas of the game, as the new pipeline comes with less overhead. However, this is just the beginning. Our initial goal was to get this pipeline working in tandem with the original pipeline to ensure everything worked correctly and that we could still switch between them at runtime. Once we have fully transitioned, we will be able to optimise this pipeline further, meaning there will be more performance gains in the near future. We also have plans for improving the quality of graphics in the game where we weren’t previously able to do due to the old pipeline.

The Rust Render Pipeline can be toggled via a setting under the experimental tab so players can switch back and forth between pipelines in case there are any issues initially. This setting is only going to be here for the first month in case anyone encounters graphical or performance issues that we missed while testing. Hopefully, after the next patch, we’ll be able to remove this fully and have RRP as the default once we know that no serious issues remain.
Anticheat: Additional Secure Servers
Back in March we introduced the ability for servers to require TPM + Secure Boot , enabling it for 6 of our own servers.

Over the last 6+ months we have seen security feature adoption grow at a steady pace and we're ready to switch more servers to secure, continuing with the following Facepunch servers:
  • [US East] Facepunch 1
  • [EA] Facepunch 1
  • [EU] Facepunch 15
  • [EU East] Facepunch 1
  • [EU] Facepunch 16
  • [EA] Facepunch 2

Our desired goal is still to make it global for all servers in Rust, but we still have some ways to go for adoption, see adoption rates over the last 6+ months:
If your hardware supports it, we would strongly recommend you take steps to enable these features, see this support page . If you have TPM and Secure Boot already enabled feel free to give a secure server a chance, we were able to determine a reduced cheater presence on these servers a month after release.
Crash uploading
Last month we fixed EAC preventing the game from dumping crashes. This month we added uploading of crashes to our backend automatically. We now get a direct report when it happens instead of having to chase down players and manually reproduce the crash in our development builds of the game.

You should see increased game stability going forward as we can respond to crashes much more effectively now.

item.title: Breach and Clear
item.description:
This month's update brings you Monument Blockers, Breakable Attack Heli Armour, HQM Nodes, Upkeep Group Scaling, various item buffs, and QoL and balance changes, as well as many performance updates and much more!

03 September 2026
DEVBLOG
Monument blockers

Monument blockers are a new obstacle we're adding to monuments with red keycard puzzle rooms. They’re intended to slow down early access to the loot at these monuments. They require a significant amount of damage to destroy but once destroyed they won't respawn. You may also find a handful of weaker monument blockers which can be destroyed by melee.

We don't think this will have an enormous impact on progression speed but it might make the early wipe a little more interesting for the first joiners.

In the event they aren’t destroyed within the first 24 hours, they will start to decay.

Upkeep group scaling

Starting this month Tool Cupboards will now apply an additional upkeep tax based on the number of players that are in a base. When calculating that number we consider a few things:

  • Any players directly authed on the TC
  • Any players that have been deauthed from the TC in the last 24 hours
  • Any players that are authed on a code lock in the base (including guest code access)
  • Any players that were deauthed from a code lock in the last 24 hours
The upkeep rates are tiered based on number of players:
  • First 4 players incur no tax
  • Next 6 players incur 2% tax per player
  • Subsequent players incur 4% tax per player
    This means a TC with 6 players authed will have +4% upkeep, a TC with 12 players will have +20% upkeep. There is a maximum tax amount of 300%. You can see the current tax rate being applied by hovering over the upkeep cost while the TC is open.

Large player groups are a tricky game balance problem to tackle as they essentially bypass most difficulty mechanics in the game via sheer numbers. We don't want to make this an unviable playstyle - Rust is a sandbox best played with friends and we believe you should be able to play it as you see fit.

We're hoping this adds an interesting problem for large groups to solve that doesn't come at the expense of small groups and solos as we believe these groups don't really have many interesting gameplay problems to tackle.

As usual, we'll monitor this over time and make adjustments as necessary. Server owners will find a set of ConVars in the Decay class that can be used to modify these behaviours, including disabling it entirely.


HQM node and collectable
High quality metal ore nodes and collectables can now be found across the island. They're extremely scarce, but you'll have more luck finding the HQM node in the Jungle.
Marketplace Power
The Drone marketplace is now connected to last months Power Plant system , requiring the server to keep the power plant up and running in order to operate drone deliveries. The marketplace now has a built in power level that slowly increases when 4 or more fuses are active in the Power Plant.

Once the battery hits 50% it can start accepting purchases. As long as at least one fuse is inserted into the Power Plant the battery won't decrease, but if it drops below 50% then the marketplace will deactivate again.

You can see the current charge level from the marketplace map screen.


Medical Honey bandage
The Medical Honey Bandage is a brand-new healing item on the Workbench Level 1. Designed to bridge the gap between the regular Bandage and Medical Syringe, it gives aspiring beekeepers another way to put their honey reserves to good use. Players with thriving bee farms often end up with more honey than they know what to do with, so we hope this new item makes the surplus feel a little sweeter.
attack Heli/HAB conditional Armour
We’ve heard your feedback - the Attack Helicopter is too difficult to counter.

Attack helicopters' existing cockpit armour will now fall off in stages as it becomes damaged, exposing both the pilot and gunner. Pilots will now have to be more careful with how close they fly to the sun.

Attack heli armour conditions

  • 80% Left panel - 680hp
  • 70% Right panel - 595hp
  • 60% Front panel - 510hp
We can't forget about the armoured HABs though, these will also have conditional armour.

Armoured HAB armour conditions

  • 90% Left panel - 2250hp
  • 80% Right panel - 2000hp
  • 70% Back panel - 1750hp
  • 60% Front panel - 1500hp
We'll being monitoring your feedback as always.
Modular car handling improvements
We've given a little bit of love to how modular cars handle. The steering, turning and suspension have all been tweaked to feel better. We have hopefully also improved how well they drive for players with higher latency.

As well as that, we have also added a handbrake mechanic, you can activate it by pressing your CTRL key. Now you will be able to do hairpin turns, take tighter corners, drift, and even do some doughnuts.

RADWATER Sprinkler BUFF
Yes: we are buffing Radwater again. This time we've given it a large buff when used in Sprinklers, specifically against those with armour.
Radwater will now seep through more armour types, causing significant radiation to those in full kits, or lower radiation protection gear. Hazmats are still an effective counter.
SAM SITE bUFFED VS DRONES
The SAM site will now do a much better job of destroying hostile drones.

Missiles will fly faster vs drones and have a larger detonation fuse area, meaning drones get taken down much more reliably.
Notable Changes
We've made several smaller balance changes across the board this month, some addressing community pain points.
Heavy Plate Helmet noise suppression
The heavy plate helmet now suppresses noise when worn. We've also increased the crafting costs.
Heavy Plate Armour movement sounds
Players wearing the Heavy Plate Jacket or Pants will now make noise when moving, audible to other players.
Better Swamp Trees
The wood harvest from swamp trees has been significantly increased to be in line with other types of trees.
Semi-Pistol damage falloff
The damage falloff has been increased, meaning less damage at range. We've also increased the crafting cost.
Pie buffs
Various pies have had their durations extended and recipes adjusted. The Hunters pie bleed reduction has increased.
Smaller Grenades Stacks
Stack sizes have been reduced to 3 for the F1, Bee Grenade, Molotov and Flashbangs. Beancans have been set to 4.
Faster Lock-on
The homing launcher lock-on duration has been reduced, allowing for earlier firing.
More SMG bodies
SMG bodies are now minorly more common, whilst rifle bodies have seen a slight reduction.
Large Medkit Radiation removal
The Large Medkit now remove radiation to match the behavior of Medical Syringes.
Updated Composter UI
You can now see how quickly things will take to turn into fertilizer, your crops will thank you.
Flashlight Remake
Let there be light!
This month, the flashlight has received a new update - featuring a brand new high quality model, high resolution textures, and new animations.  We've also updated the functionality, r/click to turn on/off, just like the torches. You'll even get a different admire animation, based on whether it's on or off!
Arrow Revamp
Arrows have had a facelift. Wooden arrows have now been updated to have more visual interest (complete with new fletching) and to feel more "RUST".

Under the hood, it's been a fiddly one, as each existing weapon contained the arrow mesh directly, so updated rigs and prefabs were required.

If this felt like dejavu, you're right. We accidentally left it in the last dev blog. It's in-game this time, we promise.
New Workshop Skinnable: Wood Armor
This month’s workshop skinnable is all four pieces of Wood Armor:

  • Wood Chestplate
  • Wood Armor Pants
  • Wood Armor Helmet
  • Wood Armor Gloves

Branching out to all four Wood Armor pieces this month we’re pining for the community to spruce up the workshop!
To make your own Wood Armor skins, head over to the in-game workshop and leaf through the Wood Armor attire items listed above. From there, you can download the model files and add your own materials and make something tree-mendous.
Crystal ASsault Rifle DLC

Machined from the toughest gemstones, this Assault Rifle skin will show each and every shot you take.

Available in 5 unique colour variations, the Crystal Assault Rifle shows the ammunition in the magazine and the inner workings as you fire.

The Crystal Assault Rifle can be purchased in-game or from the Rust Steam item store

New World Models
It's about time world models have a bit of love. This month, we're introducing over 70 new world models to replace the burlap sack.
We made sure they perform just as well as (if not better than) the burlap sack, covering dropped items ranging from electrical components to clothing.
Network Range AUdit
Lots of the entities in the world are usually networked way before they can be seen by players. Sometimes this happens too far out, so if a player was running through a specific grid: they may be getting network data about entities which they likely won't be super close to. These all add up: resulting in extra network overhead for the client + server.

A few months ago we rolled out a system that would allow us to have custom network ranges for specific objects: close, standard, far. This has only been setup for the very worst offenders, but now I've had a proper audit of most of our entities and set a huge amount of entities (around 300)  to that 'close' network range. This affects things like signs, mushrooms, driftwood etc, greatly reducing our overhead.

This won't affect gameplay, and nothing has been reduced which is rendered very far in the distance. We hope to be able to better use this system in the future, but this is a great start.
Random skin crafting
There's a new "random" skin option at the start of the skin list. With this selected, each craft of that item will get a random, unlocked skin applied.
This is saved per item, so you can have it activated for some items and keep other items with a specific skin selected.
New Navmesh
We introduced a completely new navmesh in a previous patch, disabled by default, accessible by booting servers with the -useNewNavmesh command line parameter.

We since improved performance a lot, reduced the save sizes, and squashed a lot of bugs.

This patch we are going to enable it on some of our servers and monitor how it performs.
The goal is to make it the default as a hotfix or as part of next patch if everything goes well.

What you can expect as a player:
  • maybe some animals will enter your base or get in monuments
What you can expect as a server owner:
  • navmesh is saved to disk and loaded when the server restarts, potentially leading to faster boots
  • the continuous runtime cost of NPC navigation is lighter on the main thread but uses more background threads
This is part of a push to improve performance and stability of NPCs in the long term, but also to have the option to have various NPCs navigate player bases correctly.
Improved Server Event Saving
Most Rust servers follow a daily restart schedule, to help with server stability and performance.
These restarts should ideally be fast and not affect gameplay in any way, so players can just keep going about their business after rejoining.

Until now, this wasn't the case with some of the game's biggest events, such as oil rig - if you happened to be taking rig at an unlucky time and got interrupted by the server going down, all of the loot crates and most importantly, the hackable locked crate would just disappear.

This month I've been working on fixing these kinds of issues by improving the way the server saves and loads the state of these events. Affected are the oil rigs, cargo ship, patrol helicopter, Bradley and satellite crash sites.
Paint Brush Visualizer
A new option has been added to the painting UI that projects the current paintbrush onto the object you are painting! This should help out a lot when you're painting with different brush sizes and textures at varying zoom levels.
Water Treatment Plant Maintainable Mini Rework
The pressurized tank and gearboxes in water treatment plant have received a mini rework for simplification.

Each gearbox turned fully will provide 3 hours real time of water flow to the pipes. The maximum pressure of the tank when both gearboxes are turned is enough to keep the pipes operational for, you guessed it, 6 hours.

In addition, the amount of water produced by the pipes now scales linearly with the amount of pressure in the tank. You can check the pressure at the maintenance hut where the ground-floor gearbox is.

When the tank runs out of pressure and no water is being produced, the pipes around the map will now start to lose water as well.

To compensate for some losses, the IO output has been increased. The numbers should balance out to be one water pipe being roughly equivalent to 2 pumps, with better IO push rates. The amount of pipes on the map has also been increased and should be more consistently placed.
Performance - Physics Improvements
We've customized the physics engine (PhysX) further this month, tailoring it more and more to Rust. We've added an entirely new broadphase mode, using a BVH structure that we've also applied to the underlying structures used for physics queries.

In simple terms, the old implementations for these used to scale with the number of colliders in the world which is constantly growing during a wipe cycle. Now these scale more with the number of changes that are being made which scales more with the number of active players and at a much better rate.

The data above is comparing the weekend before updating the physics engine and the weekend after, on this particular server it doubled performance.

As always, the server will get the most benefit from these changes as it's generally just doing a lot more. However, the client will always get a benefit from these changes as well.
Performance - Scripting Multithreading
One of the core rules of Unity is that you have to call scripting APIs from the main thread. So things like accessing a gameobject's transform or even accessing current time (Time.time) has to be done on main thread. This makes it very awkward and sometimes limiting to push parallelization into the game code.

But Unity enforces these checks only in Editor and debug build environments - Release builds strip out these checks for performance reasons. So we could technically write code for editor that plays by the rules, while in Release plays fast-and-dangerously, but that would be a giant headache to validate and debug.

This month me and octo found a way to trick Unity into thinking any thread to be a main thread. This allows us to unify implementations and test things in editor with confidence. This opens the door to speed up parts of code that weren't available before - but this isn't free lunch, Unity can have internal synchronization or design that doesn't assume that it'll be interacted with concurrently (which can lead to bugs). And we still need to amend code to benefit from it.

For technical details to other unity devs/users, it's a 2 step process - there's an editor-only managed code side check (Object.EnsureRunningOnMainThread) that can be replaced with a dud, and there's a native memory TLS variable that can be set from 0 to 1 to tell unity "this is a main thread" (which one can identify by scanning all TLS variables on main thread and looking to ones storing 1). Different builds and platforms will have different TLS locations, as well as memory protections to modify memory directly.

Improving Parallel Server Occlusion Generation

To test it, I trialled it out on Server Occlusion generation - there's a couple phases that the process goes through, and certain steps are easy to parallelize. Those are: sampling unity's terrain mesh heights and filtering physics query results if they have a component. In both cases it's 2 single line loops.

Before: 44s for 4.5k world - only the orange blocks have native thread parallelism, so I didn't include managed worker threads display

After: 22s for 4.5k world - the blue scatter plot bellow are all managed worker threads being busy
To be fair, it's not exactly apples to apples comparison - I've tweaked a couple things that gave 8s of speedup on it's own, so the actual speedup we got from using async tasks is 37s -> 22s .

Also, that whole "no free lunch" line - Unity, sadly, has a bunch of synchronization in play that strangles performance:
In the future I hope to engage it in more places, but it'll be a gradual process.

Mutex Pool Deprecation

While working on a new Pool implementation I've kept around original Mutex pool as a fallback. I haven't heard of any issues this month, so with this patch I'm treating it as deprecated and it will be removed in the next patch.
Salvaged hammer refresh
The hammer was another model looking very dated, so we've given it a refresh. The new high-quality model features high-resolution textures, and a new set of animations.
Performance - Memory improvements

We've made a variety of memory improvements this month across many parts of the game:

  • Reduced the memory usage of a lot of objects in the world, by very small amounts on each object but it adds up to about 15k less objects/10mb of memory
  • Reduced the texture size of many ambient occlusion textures resulting in a reduction of ~630mb, with almost no visual difference, this would affect VRAM usage.
  • Reduced the texture size of distant objects, more VRAM saving
We've also identified a few more areas to improve that we should be able to implement next month.

Early testing is showing a healthy memory saving of over 0.5GB but this will vary between machines.
Performance - Vehicle Pooling
Vehicles cause a lot of stutters when you're just roaming the world, unlike other entities - vehicles currently get fully destroyed and recreated whenever they're outside of your network range, this can cause really bad stutters somewhere in the range of 20-30ms which is longer than a couple of frames depending on your framerate.

Pooling is used on most other entities, instead of fully destroying an entity and recreating it, we just disable them and re-use them as needed. With the complexity of vehicles, especially the modular ones, it took a lot longer to get pooling working without any major issues popping up.
The new profiles are from me moving out of range and coming into range of all of the vehicles in the game, the left over spikes in the bottom screenshot are just from editor code.

Overall, you should see a lot less noticeable stutters playing the game, there is still more work to be done with pooling for things like player boats. That might be my next area to look into.
Demo Improvements
The new UI has been getting a lot of fixes and improvements based on feedback from our internal trailer team as well as the community. This month's update brings you Monument Blockers, Breakable Attack Heli Armour, HQM Nodes, Upkeep Group Scaling, various item buffs, and QoL and balance changes, as well as many performance updates and much more!

03 September 2026
DEVBLOG
Monument blockers

Monument blockers are a new obstacle we're adding to monuments with red keycard puzzle rooms. They’re intended to slow down early access to the loot at these monuments. They require a significant amount of damage to destroy but once destroyed they won't respawn. You may also find a handful of weaker monument blockers which can be destroyed by melee.

We don't think this will have an enormous impact on progression speed but it might make the early wipe a little more interesting for the first joiners.

In the event they aren’t destroyed within the first 24 hours, they will start to decay.

Upkeep group scaling

Starting this month Tool Cupboards will now apply an additional upkeep tax based on the number of players that are in a base. When calculating that number we consider a few things:

  • Any players directly authed on the TC
  • Any players that have been deauthed from the TC in the last 24 hours
  • Any players that are authed on a code lock in the base (including guest code access)
  • Any players that were deauthed from a code lock in the last 24 hours
The upkeep rates are tiered based on number of players:
  • First 4 players incur no tax
  • Next 6 players incur 2% tax per player
  • Subsequent players incur 4% tax per player
    This means a TC with 6 players authed will have +4% upkeep, a TC with 12 players will have +20% upkeep. There is a maximum tax amount of 300%. You can see the current tax rate being applied by hovering over the upkeep cost while the TC is open.

Large player groups are a tricky game balance problem to tackle as they essentially bypass most difficulty mechanics in the game via sheer numbers. We don't want to make this an unviable playstyle - Rust is a sandbox best played with friends and we believe you should be able to play it as you see fit.

We're hoping this adds an interesting problem for large groups to solve that doesn't come at the expense of small groups and solos as we believe these groups don't really have many interesting gameplay problems to tackle.

As usual, we'll monitor this over time and make adjustments as necessary. Server owners will find a set of ConVars in the Decay class that can be used to modify these behaviours, including disabling it entirely.


HQM node and collectable
High quality metal ore nodes and collectables can now be found across the island. They're extremely scarce, but you'll have more luck finding the HQM node in the Jungle.
Marketplace Power
The Drone marketplace is now connected to last months Power Plant system , requiring the server to keep the power plant up and running in order to operate drone deliveries. The marketplace now has a built in power level that slowly increases when 4 or more fuses are active in the Power Plant.

Once the battery hits 50% it can start accepting purchases. As long as at least one fuse is inserted into the Power Plant the battery won't decrease, but if it drops below 50% then the marketplace will deactivate again.

You can see the current charge level from the marketplace map screen.


Medical Honey bandage
The Medical Honey Bandage is a brand-new healing item on the Workbench Level 1. Designed to bridge the gap between the regular Bandage and Medical Syringe, it gives aspiring beekeepers another way to put their honey reserves to good use. Players with thriving bee farms often end up with more honey than they know what to do with, so we hope this new item makes the surplus feel a little sweeter.
attack Heli/HAB conditional Armour
We’ve heard your feedback - the Attack Helicopter is too difficult to counter.

Attack helicopters' existing cockpit armour will now fall off in stages as it becomes damaged, exposing both the pilot and gunner. Pilots will now have to be more careful with how close they fly to the sun.

Attack heli armour conditions

  • 80% Left panel - 680hp
  • 70% Right panel - 595hp
  • 60% Front panel - 510hp
We can't forget about the armoured HABs though, these will also have conditional armour.

Armoured HAB armour conditions

  • 90% Left panel - 2250hp
  • 80% Right panel - 2000hp
  • 70% Back panel - 1750hp
  • 60% Front panel - 1500hp
We'll being monitoring your feedback as always.
Modular car handling improvements
We've given a little bit of love to how modular cars handle. The steering, turning and suspension have all been tweaked to feel better. We have hopefully also improved how well they drive for players with higher latency.

As well as that, we have also added a handbrake mechanic, you can activate it by pressing your CTRL key. Now you will be able to do hairpin turns, take tighter corners, drift, and even do some doughnuts.

RADWATER Sprinkler BUFF
Yes: we are buffing Radwater again. This time we've given it a large buff when used in Sprinklers, specifically against those with armour.
Radwater will now seep through more armour types, causing significant radiation to those in full kits, or lower radiation protection gear. Hazmats are still an effective counter.
SAM SITE bUFFED VS DRONES
The SAM site will now do a much better job of destroying hostile drones.

Missiles will fly faster vs drones and have a larger detonation fuse area, meaning drones get taken down much more reliably.
Notable Changes
We've made several smaller balance changes across the board this month, some addressing community pain points.
Heavy Plate Helmet noise suppression
The heavy plate helmet now suppresses noise when worn. We've also increased the crafting costs.
Heavy Plate Armour movement sounds
Players wearing the Heavy Plate Jacket or Pants will now make noise when moving, audible to other players.
Better Swamp Trees
The wood harvest from swamp trees has been significantly increased to be in line with other types of trees.
Semi-Pistol damage falloff
The damage falloff has been increased, meaning less damage at range. We've also increased the crafting cost.
Pie buffs
Various pies have had their durations extended and recipes adjusted. The Hunters pie bleed reduction has increased.
Smaller Grenades Stacks
Stack sizes have been reduced to 3 for the F1, Bee Grenade, Molotov and Flashbangs. Beancans have been set to 4.
Faster Lock-on
The homing launcher lock-on duration has been reduced, allowing for earlier firing.
More SMG bodies
SMG bodies are now minorly more common, whilst rifle bodies have seen a slight reduction.
Large Medkit Radiation removal
The Large Medkit now remove radiation to match the behavior of Medical Syringes.
Updated Composter UI
You can now see how quickly things will take to turn into fertilizer, your crops will thank you.
Flashlight Remake
Let there be light!
This month, the flashlight has received a new update - featuring a brand new high quality model, high resolution textures, and new animations.  We've also updated the functionality, r/click to turn on/off, just like the torches. You'll even get a different admire animation, based on whether it's on or off!
Arrow Revamp
Arrows have had a facelift. Wooden arrows have now been updated to have more visual interest (complete with new fletching) and to feel more "RUST".

Under the hood, it's been a fiddly one, as each existing weapon contained the arrow mesh directly, so updated rigs and prefabs were required.

If this felt like dejavu, you're right. We accidentally left it in the last dev blog. It's in-game this time, we promise.
New Workshop Skinnable: Wood Armor
This month’s workshop skinnable is all four pieces of Wood Armor:

  • Wood Chestplate
  • Wood Armor Pants
  • Wood Armor Helmet
  • Wood Armor Gloves

Branching out to all four Wood Armor pieces this month we’re pining for the community to spruce up the workshop!
To make your own Wood Armor skins, head over to the in-game workshop and leaf through the Wood Armor attire items listed above. From there, you can download the model files and add your own materials and make something tree-mendous.
Crystal ASsault Rifle DLC

Machined from the toughest gemstones, this Assault Rifle skin will show each and every shot you take.

Available in 5 unique colour variations, the Crystal Assault Rifle shows the ammunition in the magazine and the inner workings as you fire.

The Crystal Assault Rifle can be purchased in-game or from the Rust Steam item store

New World Models
It's about time world models have a bit of love. This month, we're introducing over 70 new world models to replace the burlap sack.
We made sure they perform just as well as (if not better than) the burlap sack, covering dropped items ranging from electrical components to clothing.
Network Range AUdit
Lots of the entities in the world are usually networked way before they can be seen by players. Sometimes this happens too far out, so if a player was running through a specific grid: they may be getting network data about entities which they likely won't be super close to. These all add up: resulting in extra network overhead for the client + server.

A few months ago we rolled out a system that would allow us to have custom network ranges for specific objects: close, standard, far. This has only been setup for the very worst offenders, but now I've had a proper audit of most of our entities and set a huge amount of entities (around 300)  to that 'close' network range. This affects things like signs, mushrooms, driftwood etc, greatly reducing our overhead.

This won't affect gameplay, and nothing has been reduced which is rendered very far in the distance. We hope to be able to better use this system in the future, but this is a great start.
Random skin crafting
There's a new "random" skin option at the start of the skin list. With this selected, each craft of that item will get a random, unlocked skin applied.
This is saved per item, so you can have it activated for some items and keep other items with a specific skin selected.
New Navmesh
We introduced a completely new navmesh in a previous patch, disabled by default, accessible by booting servers with the -useNewNavmesh command line parameter.

We since improved performance a lot, reduced the save sizes, and squashed a lot of bugs.

This patch we are going to enable it on some of our servers and monitor how it performs.
The goal is to make it the default as a hotfix or as part of next patch if everything goes well.

What you can expect as a player:
  • maybe some animals will enter your base or get in monuments
What you can expect as a server owner:
  • navmesh is saved to disk and loaded when the server restarts, potentially leading to faster boots
  • the continuous runtime cost of NPC navigation is lighter on the main thread but uses more background threads
This is part of a push to improve performance and stability of NPCs in the long term, but also to have the option to have various NPCs navigate player bases correctly.
Improved Server Event Saving
Most Rust servers follow a daily restart schedule, to help with server stability and performance.
These restarts should ideally be fast and not affect gameplay in any way, so players can just keep going about their business after rejoining.

Until now, this wasn't the case with some of the game's biggest events, such as oil rig - if you happened to be taking rig at an unlucky time and got interrupted by the server going down, all of the loot crates and most importantly, the hackable locked crate would just disappear.

This month I've been working on fixing these kinds of issues by improving the way the server saves and loads the state of these events. Affected are the oil rigs, cargo ship, patrol helicopter, Bradley and satellite crash sites.
Paint Brush Visualizer
A new option has been added to the painting UI that projects the current paintbrush onto the object you are painting! This should help out a lot when you're painting with different brush sizes and textures at varying zoom levels.
Water Treatment Plant Maintainable Mini Rework
The pressurized tank and gearboxes in water treatment plant have received a mini rework for simplification.

Each gearbox turned fully will provide 3 hours real time of water flow to the pipes. The maximum pressure of the tank when both gearboxes are turned is enough to keep the pipes operational for, you guessed it, 6 hours.

In addition, the amount of water produced by the pipes now scales linearly with the amount of pressure in the tank. You can check the pressure at the maintenance hut where the ground-floor gearbox is.

When the tank runs out of pressure and no water is being produced, the pipes around the map will now start to lose water as well.

To compensate for some losses, the IO output has been increased. The numbers should balance out to be one water pipe being roughly equivalent to 2 pumps, with better IO push rates. The amount of pipes on the map has also been increased and should be more consistently placed.
Performance - Physics Improvements
We've customized the physics engine (PhysX) further this month, tailoring it more and more to Rust. We've added an entirely new broadphase mode, using a BVH structure that we've also applied to the underlying structures used for physics queries.

In simple terms, the old implementations for these used to scale with the number of colliders in the world which is constantly growing during a wipe cycle. Now these scale more with the number of changes that are being made which scales more with the number of active players and at a much better rate.

The data above is comparing the weekend before updating the physics engine and the weekend after, on this particular server it doubled performance.

As always, the server will get the most benefit from these changes as it's generally just doing a lot more. However, the client will always get a benefit from these changes as well.
Performance - Scripting Multithreading
One of the core rules of Unity is that you have to call scripting APIs from the main thread. So things like accessing a gameobject's transform or even accessing current time (Time.time) has to be done on main thread. This makes it very awkward and sometimes limiting to push parallelization into the game code.

But Unity enforces these checks only in Editor and debug build environments - Release builds strip out these checks for performance reasons. So we could technically write code for editor that plays by the rules, while in Release plays fast-and-dangerously, but that would be a giant headache to validate and debug.

This month me and octo found a way to trick Unity into thinking any thread to be a main thread. This allows us to unify implementations and test things in editor with confidence. This opens the door to speed up parts of code that weren't available before - but this isn't free lunch, Unity can have internal synchronization or design that doesn't assume that it'll be interacted with concurrently (which can lead to bugs). And we still need to amend code to benefit from it.

For technical details to other unity devs/users, it's a 2 step process - there's an editor-only managed code side check (Object.EnsureRunningOnMainThread) that can be replaced with a dud, and there's a native memory TLS variable that can be set from 0 to 1 to tell unity "this is a main thread" (which one can identify by scanning all TLS variables on main thread and looking to ones storing 1). Different builds and platforms will have different TLS locations, as well as memory protections to modify memory directly.

Improving Parallel Server Occlusion Generation

To test it, I trialled it out on Server Occlusion generation - there's a couple phases that the process goes through, and certain steps are easy to parallelize. Those are: sampling unity's terrain mesh heights and filtering physics query results if they have a component. In both cases it's 2 single line loops.

Before: 44s for 4.5k world - only the orange blocks have native thread parallelism, so I didn't include managed worker threads display

After: 22s for 4.5k world - the blue scatter plot bellow are all managed worker threads being busy
To be fair, it's not exactly apples to apples comparison - I've tweaked a couple things that gave 8s of speedup on it's own, so the actual speedup we got from using async tasks is 37s -> 22s .

Also, that whole "no free lunch" line - Unity, sadly, has a bunch of synchronization in play that strangles performance:
In the future I hope to engage it in more places, but it'll be a gradual process.

Mutex Pool Deprecation

While working on a new Pool implementation I've kept around original Mutex pool as a fallback. I haven't heard of any issues this month, so with this patch I'm treating it as deprecated and it will be removed in the next patch.
Salvaged hammer refresh
The hammer was another model looking very dated, so we've given it a refresh. The new high-quality model features high-resolution textures, and a new set of animations.
Performance - Memory improvements

We've made a variety of memory improvements this month across many parts of the game:

  • Reduced the memory usage of a lot of objects in the world, by very small amounts on each object but it adds up to about 15k less objects/10mb of memory
  • Reduced the texture size of many ambient occlusion textures resulting in a reduction of ~630mb, with almost no visual difference, this would affect VRAM usage.
  • Reduced the texture size of distant objects, more VRAM saving
We've also identified a few more areas to improve that we should be able to implement next month.

Early testing is showing a healthy memory saving of over 0.5GB but this will vary between machines.
Performance - Vehicle Pooling
Vehicles cause a lot of stutters when you're just roaming the world, unlike other entities - vehicles currently get fully destroyed and recreated whenever they're outside of your network range, this can cause really bad stutters somewhere in the range of 20-30ms which is longer than a couple of frames depending on your framerate.

Pooling is used on most other entities, instead of fully destroying an entity and recreating it, we just disable them and re-use them as needed. With the complexity of vehicles, especially the modular ones, it took a lot longer to get pooling working without any major issues popping up.
The new profiles are from me moving out of range and coming into range of all of the vehicles in the game, the left over spikes in the bottom screenshot are just from editor code.

Overall, you should see a lot less noticeable stutters playing the game, there is still more work to be done with pooling for things like player boats. That might be my next area to look into.
Demo Improvements
The new UI has been getting a lot of fixes and improvements based on feedback from our internal trailer team as well as the community. I think it's slowly getting to a point where we can turn it on by default, until the next patch you can participate in testing it by using demo.newui 1 in the console.

As for the improvements: I fixed a bunch of UX issues with the UI, fixed undo not working with dolly camera, added a preview in dolly edit mode so you don't need to hop between the two views too often - plus a bunch of other improvements.

I also redesigned the sandbox panel to prepare it for future improvements, one of those future improvements is parenting which is already in this update. You can parent lights to players at the moment, in the future you'll be able to parent more things to each other.

There's also a new curve editor to allow you to animate keyframes with a lot more freedom, you can use it with dolly cameras to create speed ramping or slow the camera down as it sweeps through.
I'm looking forward to seeing what people create!

item.title: Power Trip
item.description:
This month's update brings you Player Maintained Monuments in the form of a new Satellite Crash, Dome Pumping, restorable Power Plant, plus more. As well as plenty of balances, bug fixes, optimisations, upgrades, and more improvements!

06 August 2026
DEVBLOG
⠀
Player Maintained Monuments
This month we're releasing a set of features we call Player Maintained Monuments - tying together our existing monuments in new and interesting ways while pushing players to interact with each other in the process.
Powering up the power plant
Using new Heavy Fuses, the power plant can be fired back up to unlock several new gameplay features for everyone around the island.
Heavy Fuses can be found as loot and must be inserted into the new special fuse boxes located at the power plant. Not everything will be unlocked all at once - some things connected to the power plant require more fuses than others to become functional.
Once the power plant has started providing power, the powerline poles with transformers (the white cylinder-looking things) which appear alongside roads can now provide power for electrical circuits. These powerlines can also now be climbed - no need for a ladder, just approach the powerline and jump.
Green recyclers (the ones outside of safezones) have received a 10% nerf to their baseline efficiency of 50%, being restored to 60% with sufficient power from the power plant and additionally receiving a duration buff from 5s to 4.5s once the power plant is at maximum power. Yellow recyclers (inside safezones) remain unchanged from their previous behaviour. We have also added a single special new red recycler with 75% efficiency to the power plant, only usable at maximum power.
satellite crash
A new in-game event!

Power up the new Satellite Control Computer at the Launch Site with an aiming module and then take control of a satellite of your choosing.


Use the thruster buttons to target the crash location before locking it in. It doesn't come with a manual though, so you'll have to figure out which thruster button does what, first!

Once locked in, the satellite will start its descent, visible to all players on the server. After a short while it will impact and spill its new satellite loot crates.

Once they've cooled down, they're ready to loot - but the whole server knows about them too!
Dome pumping
Once the Power Plant is running, a new switch on the Large Oil Rig will become usable. This controls the flow of crude oil to Dome. Once activated, this will pump Crude for 20 minutes.

However, you can't retrieve it by yourself - you'll need to use the Tanker vehicle module to drain the oil and then transport it to a car lift to extract it.

There is also a switch on Small Oil Rig that pumps at half the rate. You can enable both switches at once to get 1.5x the Crude.
Supermarket Freezer
There is a new freezer located inside the Supermarket that provides a steady stream of chilled food so long as it is receiving power from the power plant.

Every so often, it will provide a larger food cache than usual. Happy shopping!
Water Treatment Plant Production
Water pipes will now spawn around the roadsides of the map. To start, the pipes will be empty and won't produce any water. To get them to start pumping, the Water Treatment Plant will have to be maintained.
Two gearboxes have been added inside the monument, and turning them pressurises the new intact water tank at its centre. To get a gearbox moving, the powerplant's grid needs to be live, then you'll need to place a gear into the gearbox and interact with it to start the valve wheel spinning. Gears are consumed as the wheel turns and can't be pulled back out once inserted.
When the tank reaches full pressure, the blades will start spinning and clearing up the blockages, restoring water flow across the map. After that, coming back every once in a while to keep the pressure up and the blockages clear will be much easier than a cold start.
Gas Station Car Garage
In Oxum's, the car garage has received a tune-up. When the power grid is active, or when the backup generator around the side is turned on, the garage will power up with some new features.
The garage door can be opened or closed with a switch on the outer wall, so long as that switch has power.

Inside the garage, the car lift will be operable and ready for business. Lower it down using the controls and drive a car on to start using it just like any other car lift. When you're done, raise the lift back up and head down into the cave for a chance at higher quality car part spawns!
Airfield Terminal Tower
A newly refreshed control tower has hit the airfield. On the second floor, you'll find two new terminals that charge up from fuse boxes connected to the power grid.
The smaller terminal will increase the rate at which air drops fall across the map when charged.

When the larger terminal is charged, a Chinook resupply crate can be called in to drop a crate near the airfield tarmac.

The terminals will slowly lose charge after they are activated. Once they've drained the residual charge completely, they will be available for use again.
Bar Games Pack DLC

This month we’re serving up the Bar Games Pack.

Get your buddies together and come on down to the Bar Games Pack. Featuring the unique and complex mini-games Pool and Darts, and a range of bar game-themed items to turn any base into the hottest joint in town.

Both the Pool Table and the Dart board are self-contained mini-games for both solo and multiplayer fun. Deploy them in your base, interact and play them in real-time, setting your score for others to beat.

The Pool Table allows one/two players to have a classic game of pool! It can be placed down as a normal deployable. Players will then walk around the table, jump on to get ready to hit the cue ball and pick their desired power amount before flicking their mouse up to shoot. Standard pool rules apply!

Other items include an interactive Juke Box deployable, skins for the Mini Fridge and Shotgun Trap, unique bar stools seating, and themed wallpapers and sprays.

The Bar Games Pack can be purchased in-game or from the Rust Steam item store .
Stone Sculpture iTEM DLC

On the pedestal these words appear:

“My name is Oxidemandias, king of grubs:

Look on my works, ye Mighty and despair!”

Leave a lasting legacy with the Stone Sculpture. This interactive deployable lets you carve away at stone until you create the shape of your heart’s desire. Or just sculpt your favourite appendage. Either is a surefire way to stand proud.


The Stone Sculpture can be purchased in-game or from the Rust Steam item store.
Respawn point improvements
You can now toggle a respawn option (bag/bed/etc) to display on the compass. Only one can be marked at once, and you need to interact with the bag directly to enable it. The thinking is that this will free up the standard "home" map marker.
You can also now Favourite bags on the death screen, these bags will appear first in the respawn list.
RECYCLE BIN WORKBENCH UPGRADE... UPGRADE

The Recycle Bin workbench upgrade got an upgrade of its own!

It now has its own inventory, which can be accessed by interacting with the bin itself.

All bonus items returned by the Recycle Bin upgrade now go directly into this new inventory, ready for you to collect at your convenience!

It's take-only though, so you can't fill it with loot yourself.

Nodes in safe zones
Ore nodes and woodpiles can no longer spawn in safe zones.

As they could only be harvested using a rock, they tended to pile up and eventually drained the global spawn population, preventing new nodes from appearing elsewhere on the map.
Wolf Headdress Balance & QOL
The Wolf Headdress has always been a strong option early and mid wipe, providing good head protection and the ability to be combined with a bandana. To give other helmets a chance as a viable alternative in early bow fights, we have decided to lock its crafting behind needing a Tier 1 workbench.

Also, a quality of life improvement is coming to the lunar new year animal masks. These have always had the same stats as the Wolf Headdress, and have now been set up as skins, allowing you to freely re-skin between all of the variants, and avoiding clutter in the crafting menu.
Toggling Shields
You can now swap between having the shield on your back and aiming down sights vs. having it to the side and blocking with it.

To do so, go to your settings panel and set up the bind. Once you have it set, you can switch between the two stances every couple of seconds.


We added a cooldown to the stance switching to prevent players from spamming it - it'd lead to more randomness in gun fights rather than players strategically sticking to one stance.
High WAll upkeep
Players have found ways to claim large areas of the map by spamming deployables as long as the game has been alive, whether it's been pillars, TCs or high walls. Changes in the past have helped address this, such as upkeep and adding a sheet metal crafting cost to high stone walls. This is another step forward to reducing the effectiveness of blocking access to large areas of the map.

High walls now have a static upkeep cost of 20%. This brings them in the middle of building blocks (10% -> 33%) to keep them the intended way to make compounds while discouraging spamming them.

This makes it more expensive and a hassle to come up with enough upkeep for external TCs if you don't want to keep refilling them. It should also help clear up old compounds after a base is raided.
Water well Vendor Stock
Water wells are a great stepping stone into the world of farming by allowing you to get a taste of tea buffs and high level tools. However, over time (and especially with the extra influx of scrap from the blueprint update), more and more players started using it as an alternative to farming. In the most extreme example, you could buy 10x jackhammers and 10x advanced teas a few hours into wipe, leading to much faster progression than intended.
To return to its intended function, we kept the prices the same but reduced the stock that each water well vendor has.
  • Stock lowered from 10 -> 2
  • Restock time increased from 2m -> 10m

This should allow you to use it as a quick boost without it becoming an alternative to the intended farming progression of setting up farms and cloning plants.
Hover looting Fix
This is a "relatively minor bug" but it needed a dedicated section in the blog to explain it properly.

In Rust's inventory system, when holding ALT, it will try to move the item "onto your player".

Examples:
  • move into backpack before main inventory
  • wear clothing instead of dumping in chest
  • move from backpack to main inventory instead of dumping in chest
  • equip clothing instead of putting into main inventory
The bug was "hover looting a body bag corpse would do nothing if it needed to swap clothing". When nothing happened, you would try to hover loot again... and it still wouldn't work. Next, you would panic and try to manually swap the items.. which still wouldn't work. So finally, in the middle of the fight you would start unequipping your current armour just to be able to equip the armour off the body bag.

This is fixed so it works intuitively. It will now allow you to swap clothing despite the inventory being locked and put the clothing you are taking off into your main inventory. There is also special handling so if your inventory is completely full, it will move the clothing you are taking off into the body bag you are looting.

This should reduce frustration when looting clothing from corpses in big fights and raids.
Master key
Last month, the Master Key used in the Apartment Complex shipped without a model. Of course, none of you noticed because nobody would ever break into their poor neighbour's apartment for scraps, right?
It now has a fully functional view model and animations, so the experience of cracking open your neighbour's apartment can feel even better.
DEmo UI 2
The demo UI got a complete makeover; everything in the UI was recreated from scratch, not only to be much easier to use but also to provide powerful features for both our internal trailers and content creators.

Most of this was just done in my free time as a love letter to video game editing communities, as being a part of them when I was younger led me to working on Rust. This explains why it wasn't on any of the roadmaps.

One of the main goals of the new UI is to ease the learning curve needed to create basic content. Previously, you needed a lot of binds and console commands for even the simplest cinematics, with the new features, you should be able to access everything from the UI.

Some of the features that will help you with that are:
  • Options panel - a set of sliders and toggles that let you control the camera, depth of field, time of day and post processing.
  • Dolly camera - lets you place cameras at any point in time and sweep through them.
  • Keyframe timeline - animate any slider in the options panel to create things like cool timelapses, sweep the focus distance, etc.
  • Sandbox mode - clone players, place lights, with more features coming in the future.
  • Scene system - Do all of the above, create variations, its our equivalent of project files within a demo.
  • Change appearance - You can change the clothing and seed of any player or hide them altogether.
  • Export as a png sequence - this will be further expanded to export videos in the future.
Using the new demo UI should feel familiar to anyone who worked with video editing applications before, however, we also tried to make it intuitive to new content creators by adding tooltips and keeping the UI fairly simple.

This is the first iteration of the new demo UI, it's going to receive more features as time goes on based on both internal needs as well as community suggestions. With the new timeline and sandbox mode, we have a really solid foundation to add new tabs to the options panel in the future as well as new sandbox objects like entities.

For now, the new UI is not enabled by default and requires ` demo.newui ` to be set in the console. This is mostly to gather more feedback before we enable it by default in future updates.
New Workshop Skinnable: Small Backpack

This month’s workshop skinnable is the Small Backpack.

Our first wearable in a while, the Small Backpack should be a great receptacle for some exciting skins!

To make your own Small Backpack skin, head over to the in-game workshop and locate the Small Backpack deployable item. From there, you can download the model file and add your own materials.
Game Startup optimisations
We've improved the startup loading times.

Loading into the main menu was pulling in a lot of assets that weren't needed yet. It now only loads whats strictly required to reach the menu, with the rest streaming in the background.

On most machines this should be about twice as fast.
Server Performance Improvements

Parallel Entity Saving on Jobs 4

Currently experimental UsePlayerUpdateJobs 4 mode is gaining a pretty important feature - fully parallel saving of entities, which should ease up one of the main bottlenecks in a server's frame processing.

Back in Jobs 2 era I've introduced parallel snapshot sending. I only mentioned in passing on the blog, but the short version of what it does is:
  • Build a dependency chain of snapshots (if we send both a parent and a child snapshot, then they gotta send in order as one chain)
  • Sort chains by ones having entities to serialize vs ones without
  • Former go to main thread, latter to worker threads
Here's the most egregious example where this implementation struggled:
The entire process took 5ms, where about 2.5ms was spent on building and sorting chains into task groups(the red square). Afterwards about 13 threads were helping send data while main thread spent another 2.5ms to serialize everything.

There's no nice way to fix this, so we had to just support parallel saving if we wanted to improve things further. After making all save code thread safe, I simplified the logic - now snapshots get packaged up into batches(controlled by ParallelNetworkQueueBatchSize, def 256), each batch is it's own task for thread pool.

Our synthetic tests(256 batch size, no parenting, no caching) show following improvement:
  • 1000 entities: 6.6ms -> 3.6ms
  • 10000 entities: 64.4ms -> 10.6ms

New Pool, Take 2

Back in June update we shipped a new pool that I called "FuzzyPool". It's fast, but it has a tendency to leak a small amount of objects during high contention. I got feedback from a bunch of community devs that it's a problem for them and they had to fall back to old mutex pool.

So I rewrote it again - FuzzyPool is gone. This time instead of trying to invent it myself and have it be derpy I did some research and discovered LPRQ implementation by Raed Romanov and Nikita Koval . I repurposed one of it's internal mechanisms (PRQ) to make our pool better - it either matches FuzzyPool perf or exceeds it up to 20% in some scenarios, while also showing 0 leaks in high-contention scenarios.

Bellow you can see some graphs - less is better:
  • Mutex - our original implementation, omitted in most graphs as it breaks scale
  • FuzzyCB - current implementation of Pool
  • ConcQSegm - implementation based on CoreCLR's ConcurrentQueue shipped with unity's mscorlib
  • LPRQSegm - new implementation
If I don't hear about issues with it, then I'll rip out Mutex pool in the patch after this.
Notable Changes
Maximum Rent
Maximum stored rent at the Apartment complex is now capped at 72 hours
Attachment Sounds
Audible range of equipping a weapon attachment has been reduced from 60m to 20m
Swing ragdolling
Players will ragdoll when dismounting the Apartment Complex swing set
Kayaks and Paddles
Fishing village now sells Kayaks and Paddles, rather than the blueprint of those items
Vehicle Emojis
In addition to regular and item emojis, all vehicles now have their own emoji available in the in-game chat.
Along with that there have been some improvements to the emoji picker UI. Before you had to remember or guess the "short name" of the emoji you wanted to use, now it allows you to search for them by their name in your selected language.
SETFlag deprecation
For modders - we intend to remove SetFlag from the codebase with the September wipe (3rd Sep 26). We recently replaced this with a disposable pattern to encourage more efficient usage of updating entity flags.

Where before we could have a flags update look like this: 
SetFlag(Flags.Reserved1, true);
SetFlag(Flags.Reserved2, true);
SetFlag(Flags.Reserved3, true);
That would now look like this: 
using (var setFlags = StartSetFlags(FlagsUpdateMode.SendNetworkUpdate_Flags))
{
    setFlags.Set(Flags.Reserved1, true);
    setFlags.Set(Flags.Reserved2, true);
    setFlags.Set(Flags.Reserved3, true);
}
Community UI Updates
This month, we've done a pass of additions, improvements and fixes to the Community UI used by the modded community. This adds new CUI components, as well as a new feature and mechanic which allows server-side pie context menus.

New component: Tooltip

This adds the ability to show a tooltip when hovering over any graphic element in your CUIs.

New Component: Canvas Group

Adds the ability to change graphic alpha, blocksRaycasts and interactable - this includes all child panels of the group component object.

New Component: Mask

Adds the ability to mark an Image / RawImage as a mask, of which all child components will be masked by using the invisible alpha of the mask.

Image PPU (Pixels Per Unit)

An issue which would block users from using the Image slice property was the lack of control over the PPU variables which has been exposed with this update under "ppuMultiplier".

New Mechanic: Custom Pie Menu

This allows plugins to create a custom context menu from the server, which executes a command when an option is picked, or when the pie menu closes.

Misc Changes

  • New RPC: CommunityEntity.DestroyUIs - takes a list of panel names to destroy at once
  • Fixed: Button and Scrollbar color tweening / transition fade when it first gets created
  • Exposed: Button and InputField "interactable" individual property
  • Exposed: Individual graphics can now use "blocksRaycast" property
All source code for the changes above are available on the Rust.Community Github .
Rust OST on vinyl

The Rust Original Soundtrack is finally coming to vinyl.

For the first time, Alex Rehberg's acclaimed score has been pressed onto a deluxe triple-LP.

90 minutes of atmospheric ambient music that perfectly captures the tension, isolation and beauty of life on the island.

The deluxe set is available to pre-order now, with full details on the pressing, artwork and release available here .
